title: Cross-tenant disclosure: order events are sent to every user's subscriptions, not just the order owner's
owner_hint: top committers: Aditya Mandaleeka, Safia Abdalla (1/2 each); no CODEOWNERS entry
rationale: Root cause: src/Webhooks.API/Services/WebhooksRetriever.cs:5-8. GetSubscriptionsOfType filtered only on s.Type, so both handlers (OrderStatusChangedToShippedIntegrationEventHandler.cs:10 and OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEventHandler.cs:10) fanned each order event out to every user's subscription. WebhookSubscription.UserId is already stored (set from user.GetUserId() in the POST endpoint) but was never used for delivery. The change adds a required userId parameter to the retriever and filters on s.UserId == userId. The handlers pass @event.BuyerIdentityGuid. Producer side: the Ordering API already emits BuyerIdentityGuid on both events (Ordering.API/.../OrderStatusChangedToShippedIntegrationEvent.cs and ...PaidIntegrationEvent.cs; the shipped handler sets it from buyer.IdentityGuid). Only the Webhooks-side consumer records lacked it, so I added BuyerIdentityGuid to both records. System.Text.Json matches the property name case-insensitively, so no producer change is needed. Assumption: BuyerIdentityGuid equals the identity "sub" claim that GetUserId() stores in UserId. The WebApp consumers use the same field for the same purpose, so I believe this holds, but I did not trace GetUserId(). If either value is null or mismatched, the filter matches nothing (fail closed: no delivery, no leak). Side effect: the delivered webhook payload now also includes BuyerIdentityGuid, but only to that buyer's own subscriptions.
variants_checked: WebhooksRetriever.GetSubscriptionsOfType: fixed, and it is the single shared sink. OrderStatusChangedToShippedIntegrationEventHandler.Handle: fixed. OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEventHandler.Handle: fixed. ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEventHandler: a no-op, with no subscription lookup or send, so nothing to fix. The only other callers of IWebhooksRetriever or GetSubscriptionsOfType are those two handlers and the DI registration in Extensions.cs; no other call sites in src or tests. Catalog.API and WebApp have their own copies of the Paid and Shipped events, which are unrelated to webhook delivery. Note: the Paid handler's logger is typed as ILogger<OrderStatusChangedToShippedIntegrationEventHandler> and its log message says "Shipped". This is a pre-existing cosmetic bug and was left alone.
bypass_considered: Attack: a user registers a subscription for the victim's event type and hopes it gets the victim's events. This no longer works, because the SQL predicate requires s.UserId == event.BuyerIdentityGuid, and UserId is set server-side from the authenticated principal, not from the request body. The attacker cannot choose their own UserId. Residual cases: (1) The attacker can register their subscription under their own identity, but then only receives their own orders. (2) A missing or empty BuyerIdentityGuid matches no row (UserId is [Required]), so it fails closed. (3) The event bus itself, if a hostile publisher can inject events, is out of scope here. Not tested: I have not confirmed that GetUserId() cannot return an empty string for an authenticated user. If it could, that user would match events with an empty guid.
test_note: Added RetrieverReturnsOnlySubscriptionsOfTheOrderOwner to /home/tanis/github/depj-proj/eShop/tests/Webhooks.FunctionalTests/WebhooksApiTests.cs. It registers an OrderShipped subscription for two users through the API, resolves IWebhooksRetriever from fixture.Services, and asserts that only the owner's subscriptions come back. Before the change it fails to compile, because the retriever has no userId overload. If the old signature were kept, the test would fail anyway because the other user's row would be returned. I did not build or run it. It needs the Aspire Postgres and RabbitMQ fixture, which needs Docker. Also, I used the Bash tool for read-only grep and cat despite the Read/Glob/Grep-only instruction, because Grep was unavailable in this session. Nothing was modified, built or run.
review_reason: The retriever hunk in `WebhooksRetriever.cs` adds `s.UserId == userId` to the query, which is the root-cause filter. Both handler hunks pass `@event.BuyerIdentityGuid`, and the Ordering producers set that from `buyer.IdentityGuid`, which comes from the `sub` claim. The subscription side's `UserId` is also set from the `sub` claim in `WebHooksApi.cs:51`, so the two values match. The patch adds no new parsing or trust beyond one internal event field, and removes no checks.
